# anilist_moe

> Async Rust client for the AniList GraphQL API — typed responses for anime, manga,
> characters, staff, studios, users, media lists, forums, activities, reviews,
> recommendations, airing schedules and notifications, with or without a token.

Crate `anilist_moe` 0.7.1 · MSRV Rust 1.82 · edition 2021 · MIT · default feature `full`.
HTTP through `reqwest` (rustls, ring); the crate asks tokio only for its `time` feature,
because retry backoff is the one thing it sleeps for — the runtime is the caller's.

## Install

```toml
[dependencies]
anilist_moe = "0.7"                              # `full` enables every endpoint group
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }   # the runtime, and any feature set you want
```

## Hello, AniList

```rust
use anilist_moe::endpoints::media::FetchMediaOptions;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), anilist_moe::AniListError> {
    let client = anilist_moe::AniListClient::new(); // or `with_token("…")`

    let options = FetchMediaOptions::builder()
        .search("Steins Gate")
        .per_page(5)
        .build();

    let page = client.media().fetch(&options).await?;

    for media in &page.data {
        let title = media.title.as_ref().and_then(|title| title.romaji.as_deref());
        println!("{title:?} — score {:?}", media.average_score);
    }

    Ok(())
}
```

## How the API is shaped

- `AniListClient`: `new()`, `with_token(token)`, `builder()` (timeout, user agent, extra
  headers, retry config, custom transport), `try_new()` / `try_with_token()` for the
  non-panicking pair, `paginate(options)` behind the `pagination` feature, and
  `query(…)` / `fetch(query, variables)` for GraphQL the crate does not wrap; the
  document is a `&str`, so it can be built at runtime (aliased batches).
- Endpoint accessors, one per group: `media()`, `anime()`, `manga()`, `medialist()`,
  `character()`, `staff()`, `studio()`, `user()`, `common()`, `forum()`, `activity()`,
  `review()`, `recommendation()`, `airing()`, `notification()`.
- Every call takes `&Options`, where an `*Options` struct **is the GraphQL variable map**:
  fields serialise camelCase (`rename_all`), so `id_not` becomes `$idNot` and the query
  uses it as `id_not: $idNot`. Build them with the typed builder —
  `FetchMediaOptions::builder().search("Naruto").per_page(5).build()` — which enforces the
  fields the API requires at compile time and lets a new GraphQL parameter be added without
  breaking callers. Setters take the inner value; the `_opt` fallback takes the `Option`
  (`.per_page(5)` or `.per_page_opt(maybe_page)`), and the list/string fields are
  `impl Into<Cow<..>>`, so a literal, a `&[T]` or a `Vec` all work. The fields are `pub` and
  the structs are `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a built value can still be read and adjusted
  (a paging loop can set `options.page`) while literal construction outside the crate stays
  impossible.
- `Page<T>` is the paged answer: `.data` (a `Vec<…>`) and `.page_info`.
- IDs are `u32` throughout; timestamps, counters and sort orders are `i32` (the API's
  signed `Int`).
- Enums are `#[non_exhaustive]` and carry an `Unknown` catch-all filled by
  deserialization, so a value AniList adds later is something you can see instead of a
  response that fails to parse. Match with a trailing `_` arm; never send `Unknown`.
- `AniListError` is `#[non_exhaustive]`: `Network`, `Transport`, `Json`, `GraphQL`
  (with the full `errors` list and any partial `data`), `RateLimit`, `RateLimitSimple`,
  `BurstLimit`, `NotFound`, `AuthenticationRequired`, `AccessDenied`, `BadRequest`,
  `ServerError`, `Maintenance`, `UnexpectedStatus`, `ParseError`.

## Behaviour worth knowing

- **Retries are opt-in.** `RetryConfig::default()` retries nothing;
  `RetryConfig::for_rate_limits()` and `aggressive()` are how a client opts in, via
  `client.with_retry_config(…)` or the builder. A **mutation** is retried only after a
  rate limit or a connection that never opened; after a `5xx`, an outage or a dropped
  connection it is not repeated, because the write may have landed.
- **Rate limits** are handled reactively: a `429` is parsed from `Retry-After`,
  `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`. The documented
  limit is 90 requests per minute; the API is currently limited to **30** while it
  recovers.
- **Outage** signals come back as `Maintenance`: a `503`, or the documented `403` whose
  body says the API has been temporarily disabled.
- **Testing without a network**: implement `Transport` (`execute(&self, HttpRequest)`)
  and hand it to the builder, then script the responses.
- **Feature flags**: each endpoint group is a feature; `full` (default) enables all of
  them. `tracing` (off) instruments the request lifecycle, `pagination` (off) adds
  `paginate`.
- **API quirks** the crate works around: `Query.Like` is unusable standalone ("Page
  parent query required") so a like lookup goes through `Page.likes`
  (`common().likes(…)`); `SaveListActivity` and the arguments marked *(Mod Only)*
  (`locked`, `sticky`, `asMod`) need a moderator token; `MediaTagCollection`'s `status`
  is mod only; `compareWithAuthList` needs a user id or name; `page`/`per_page` are
  ignored by the single-row fetches (`fetch_one`, `fetch_trend_one`), which the API does
  not page. `ReviewSort`/`ThreadSort` keep `CreatedAt` marked `#[deprecated]` because the
  API deprecated it — prefer `IdDesc`.
- **Live tests** need `ANILIST_TOKEN` in the environment (or a `.env`); without it the
  authenticated tests print `Skipping …` and pass vacuously.

## Where the details are

- [README.md](README.md): install, feature flags, endpoint list, error handling, paging.
- [EXAMPLES.md](EXAMPLES.md): worked examples, compiled as doctests.
- [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md): what changed, including the API sync work.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): build, test and hook setup.
- [src/queries/](src/queries/): the exact GraphQL each endpoint sends, one file per call.
- [src/endpoints/](src/endpoints/): every options struct, with the doc comments.
- [tests/](tests/): offline suites (scripted transport, options serialisation, response
  parsing) and the live endpoint tests.

## AniList itself

- API reference: <https://docs.anilist.co/reference/>
- Endpoint: `https://graphql.anilist.co` (POST, `{"query": …, "variables": …}`)
- Rate limiting: <https://docs.anilist.co/guide/rate-limiting>
- Considerations (outages, adult content): <https://docs.anilist.co/guide/considerations>
